title: Suika merges things to clear them. I made merging the way you build your ammo, then fire it at invaders
author: office-canard
selftext:
SMART VOID started with Suika, the watermelon game. I wanted something that feels good from the very first move, nothing clever, nothing you have to earn. Honestly, half of this game is still that one.



The other half came from one thing I noticed while playing it. When things merge, the merged thing is big, and throwing something big feels good. So in SMART VOID, merging isn't how you clear the screen. It's how you build your ammo. Then you fire it.



My first target was Breakout. But Breakout only pays off when you clear the whole screen, which is a late reward, the exact thing I was trying to avoid. So I switched to Space Invaders. A ball you've merged up big wipes out a whole cluster in one hit. The bigger you grow your shot, the bigger the payoff.



How it plays:

\- Merge balls to grow your shot, then fire it at the invaders

\- Every 10th stage is a boss, and each boss is where the next gimmick shows up first. From the next stage on, it's part of normal play

\- I wanted it calm, so the bosses teach instead of punish



The name: SMART comes from the analog feel of a smart-ball pinball table. I wanted a neon, retro-future Kowloon look, and I couldn't get the visuals anywhere near it. So I went the other way and emptied the space out. That's the VOID.



How AI fit in:

Claude wrote all of the code. There are no image files and no audio files anywhere in this game. Every graphic (the balls, the invaders, the bosses, the backgrounds, the effects) is drawn from shapes in code on an HTML canvas. All the music and sound effects are synthesized from scratch in code with the Web Audio API, no samples. It's built entirely out of code, not assets.



I never told Claude how to program anything. I described what the player should see and feel, I played every build on my phone, and when something was off (a particle that didn't show up, a color that looked too washed out, a shot that felt too slow), I'd point it out and Claude would track down the cause and fix it. That back-and-forth is how it got finished.



Free to play in your browser:

[https://office-canard.itch.io/smart-void](https://office-canard.itch.io/smart-void)
